

Finding rules version 2. A reviewer_gap is one unread work or one search that was not run. It holds kind, text, formulation, basis, need, unsettled, and exactly one of work or search. formulation is the exact statement or a declared neighbour. basis is a nonempty list of quotations {the identity fields of an excerpt, text}, each at least 20 normalized characters, copied from a verified excerpt or delivered passage, or from delivered evidence in a review of one request. need states the question about this formulation that the judgment needs answered. unsettled states why no bound reading, query or recorded search judgment answers it; explain why any exclusion reason fails. work is {title, identifiers?}; it names a work in the basis and no work already read. search is {terms, missing_term}; missing_term occurs in order in a quotation and has a content token that occurs in no bound query of this formulation. Reordering, case and punctuation do not make a gap. Tokens use NFKC, case folding and splitting at every nonletter and nondigit. finding_index.searches gives record_id, search_digest, formulations and digest references to queries, scope, dispositions, resolved and row_dispositions where present; finding_index.fields holds each value once under its digest. When the index is too long for the fixed part of a request, its longest values other than queries are not in fields, and finding_index.units gives for each, under the same digest, {unit, characters}: the handle of the body that holds the value, and its length. A passage request for that handle returns text of the body. When finding_index is {unit, characters, searches, read_works}, the whole index is the content of the body with that handle, which an earlier turn delivered. The checks use every bound query and every read work in each case. finding_index.read_works lists reading_id, reading_digest, version_id, identifiers and title. A matching normalized identifier or tokenized title means that the work is already read. The checks run in this order: gap_fields, gap_formulation, gap_basis, gap_work_read, gap_term_delivered, gap_term_bound. An index, database, language, period or unpublished literature that was not reached is a coverage limit unless delivered text supplies the named work or term and need. State limits in coverage. With supported_open possible and no ground, return supported_open. For a final over provider-refused unread ranges, cite the complete unread set in a packet_defect ground; a reviewer_gap still needs every named-gap field and check. Other kinds of ground and the three outcome rules keep their fields and meaning.
